narrative: Spend rose 15.3% to ₹12,938 (from ₹11,216) on 44 Meta purchases, up slightly from 43 — cost per purchase rose for a second straight window, up 12.7% to ₹294 (from ₹261), and CPM climbed again too, up 14.7% to ₹181.77 (from ₹158.41). Despite that, Shopify's own numbers actually accelerated: orders rose 12.5% to 54 (from 48), revenue jumped 26.0% to ₹44,279 (from ₹35,137), and ROAS improved to 3.42x (from 3.13x) — the best ROAS reading in several weeks. This split (Meta-reported cost per purchase rising while real Shopify sales grow faster) lines up with this tab's known attribution-lag pattern, where Meta's most recent days of purchases are under-reported at pull time and catch up later — worth treating the rising Meta-side CPR as likely lag rather than a genuine efficiency problem, given Shopify tells a clearly positive story.

Hook rate fell again, down 6.1% to 12.48% (from 13.29%) — a fifth consecutive read of decline, still without a clear reversal despite repeated recommendations to test a new opening frame. Frequency stayed essentially flat (1.372, from 1.374), so the saturation risk flagged weeks ago continues to ease.
